claim.text: Byte-frozen LMMSE receiver inputs under PyTorch 2.9.1 and 2.10.0 can have matching outputs on one GitHub runner; software-version difference alone does not force differing bits.
claim.scope: One GitHub-hosted Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C VM, 6 synthetic fixtures, 2 whitening settings, 3 repeats each, A1=Python3.11/Torch2.9.1, B=Python3.13/Torch2.10, A2=A1.
assumptions: same running GitHub VM for all stages
frozen complex tensor bytes checked via SHA-256
one CPU thread, CPU-only Sionna LMMSE implementation
three repeated calls per fixture and mode
matched non-Torch Python numerical package versions
forbidden_promotions: Do not claim PyTorch2.9.1 and 2.10.0 bitwise identical on all hardware
Do not infer physical 6G receiver performance
Do not infer a causal CPU driver solely from run-to-run agreement
Do not claim PyTorch alone is isolated while Python versions also differ

preregistration.prediction: If earlier discrepancies are driven by run environment rather than an unavoidable Torch-version shift, the A1-B-A2 finite outputs can match on one VM; A1=A2 should hold as the repeatability control
preregistration.primary_metric: Per fixture and repeat byte equality of raw finite output SHA (complex estimate and effective noise) with unchanged failure classification
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Exact deterministic comparisons on 6 selected cases x 2 modes x 3 repeats, one VM; no sampling confidence claim
preregistration.kill_condition: If A1 and A2 mismatch, version-only causal attribution is invalid. If input bytes mismatch, entire cross-version comparison is invalid
preregistration.stop_condition: Do not repeat without physical receiver defect or upstream maintainer request
preregistration.promotion_rule: Only the bounded measured same-host result is promoted; no universal PyTorch portability or RF performance claim

result.observed: On one Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C GitHub VM, A1-B-A2 across Python3.11/Torch2.9.1 and Python3.13/Torch2.10.0 gave exactly equal 27/27 finite repeated output pairs, 36/36 failure classifications and 36/36 Cholesky statuses in each pairwise comparison. Recomputed WSW^H bytes matched each other across both environments for all 36 comparisons but not the original frozen transported covariance bytes. All 12 moderate control repeated rows per stage pass.
result.effect_size: Zero absolute finite LMMSE estimate difference and zero absolute effective noise variance difference in all 3 comparisons; 27/27 matching finite rows per comparison; 9/9 repeated nonfinite classifications per comparison.
result.uncertainty: One VM, 6 purposively chosen fixtures, 2 whitening modes, 3 repetitions, no statistical confidence interval or representative channels. Python and Torch versions changed together; no cross-host replication of A-B-A.
retired_claims: PyTorch versions alone necessarily cause different LMMSE bits on any CPU
Seeded random fixture generation is sufficient for cross-runtime bit equality
Input byte identity by itself ensures output bit identity on arbitrary hosted CPUs
active_remainder: Which CPU architecture or dispatch differences produced separate-host bit mismatches remains unknown
Physical RF receiver relevance not measured
Stop until supported-device defect or maintainer review requires work
